sources.entry: Healthy Battery - Open-source charge limiter with live power flow and long-term battery health for Apple Silicon MacBooks. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/berkinefeavci/healthy-battery) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Free, open-source macOS menu-bar app for Apple Silicon MacBooks that sets an 80–100% charge limit, shows live power flow, and tracks long-term battery health.
summary.what_it_does: Drives macOS's native charge-limit control to hold the battery between 80% and 100% in 5% steps, with a Top Up option to charge to 100% temporarily. It shows a live diagram of adapter, battery, CPU, display and other power in watts, with CPU and display values read from Apple SMC sensors and unmeasurable values shown as "—". It keeps daily summaries for up to 400 days, with battery-health trend charts and CSV export. Additional features include power-mode switching per power source via pmset, MagSafe LED control, schedules, Apple Shortcuts actions, and a conflict guard that locks its limit writes when other charge-limit tools are present. An experimental section cuts the adapter in software to run the Mac from battery for discharge, calibration, adapter mode and sailing.
use_cases: limit battery charging to 80% to extend battery life
monitor MacBook battery health over months
see how many watts the laptop and its adapter are using
schedule power mode or charge limit changes
control MagSafe LED from the menu bar
how_to_run: Download the latest .dmg from Releases and drag Healthy Battery.app to Applications
notable: Charge limit applied through macOS's own native control, verified with an independent read-back
Live power flow with measured-only values; unmeasured values show '—' instead of estimates
Conflict guard that prevents fights with AlDente, BatFi, bclm and similar tools
Ten Apple Shortcuts actions for reading battery state and controlling limits, Top Up, discharge and power mode
No telemetry or account; signed and notarized releases; localized in five languages
caveats: Apple Silicon only; tested only on macOS 27 and a single Mac model, other versions and models are untested
Relies on Apple's private PowerUI framework, which a macOS update can break without warning
Applying a limit is a configuration write, not proof that charge current physically stops at that percentage
Through-the-adapter features are experimental and need an administrator prompt and a passing adapter test; they work only while the Mac is awake
